source_authority: Pension Fund Regulatory and Development Authority
text: The Government of India introduced the Atal Pension Yojana (APY) with effect from 1 June 2015 to support a universal social security system, especially for poor, under-privileged and unorganised-sector workers. APY is available to Indian citizens who have a savings bank account with a bank or the Department of Posts. The minimum joining age is 18 years and the maximum is 40 years. From 1 October 2022, a citizen who is or has been an income-tax payer is not eligible to join APY. The Pension Fund Regulatory and Development Authority administers APY within the National Pension System architecture. The scheme is implemented through public-sector banks, private banks, regional rural banks, small finance banks, payments banks, co-operative banks and the Department of Posts.
title: Atal Pension Yojana (APY) - PFRDA

source_authority: Pension Fund Regulatory and Development Authority
text: APY is a voluntary pension system based on periodic contributions. After age 60, a subscriber is entitled to a Central Government-guaranteed minimum pension of Rs. 1,000, Rs. 2,000, Rs. 3,000, Rs. 4,000 or Rs. 5,000 per month, according to the selected contribution plan, until the subscriber's death. After the subscriber dies, the spouse is entitled to receive the same pension amount until the spouse's death. After both the subscriber and spouse have died, the nominee is entitled to receive the pension wealth accumulated up to the subscriber's age of 60. Subscribers must make the prescribed contributions from the joining age until age 60 to receive these benefits. To join, an applicant can obtain the APY Registration Form from a bank branch or post office, complete it and submit it to the corresponding branch or post office. An interested subscriber may alternatively join online through eAPY.
title: Atal Pension Yojana (APY) - PFRDA
